Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-22

Duration: ~48 minutes
Recording: (auto) https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-2028-07-22-1132
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (BrightFind), Priya Singh (BrightFind), Noah Patel (BrightFind)

Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + rerank endpoints. Walkthrough of search relevance use case, latency tradeoffs, batching/caching suggestions from Redwood Optimize, and enterprise concerns (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Agreed next steps: pricing send, benchmark plan, sample data upload and pilot kickoff.

Topics: embeddings endpoint, rerank API, hosted vs dedicated, latency SLOs, security (SOC2/KMS), data residency / EMEA, console dashboards, Optimize recommendations, sample benchmark plan.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, i'm the ae on this account, with me is ethan our se, we'll do a quick 30 to 40 minute walkthrough of our hosted api embeddings and the rerank flow and then leave time for q's.
00:16 Liam O'Connor: hey thanks, i'm liam, head of search at brightfind. we have priya and noah on the call, we're excited to see the rerank flow for our results.
00:25 Priya Singh: hi all. quick context - we're currently using opensearch + a python embedding microservice that kicks off ada-embedding at inference time. we see sometimes stale results and high cost, so we want to understand a hosted alternative or dedicated pool.
00:40 Ethan Park: got it. real quick i want to show the typical two-step pattern we recommend - embeddings for vector store similarity then a rerank pass using our rerank endpoint which is optimized for small context and low latency. i'll also point out the console and optimize suggestions for batching and cache.
00:55 Noah Patel: curious on numbers - what's the typical latency from embeddings + rerank for a single query? we're aiming for sub 200 ms 95p.
01:06 Ethan Park: good q. for hosted api metrics you'd expect embedding creation in 30-80ms for small models (depending on batch and payload) and rerank in ~40-120ms when configured for low-latency mode; combined often in 120-220ms 95p on hosted regions in us-west/eu-west. dedicated can push that lower if you pin capacity and use larger batch windows. these are rough depends-on-workload numbers.
01:28 Liam O'Connor: that range is reasonable. cost? right now embeddings cost kills our budget when we do per-request embedding.
01:35 Maya Chen: totally - that's where Redwood Optimize comes in. we can suggest batching, prefix caching for repeated queries, and model selection/quantization tips to balance cost and latency. for hosted pricing we charge per-embedding unit and per-rerank request; i'll send the exact tiered numbers after.
01:51 Priya Singh: can you show the actual request flow? like headers, typical payload size, and what a rerank call looks like?
02:00 Ethan Park: sure, i'm going to share my screen - demo now.
02:12 [screen share: Redwood Console] 02:16 Ethan Park: here is the console - landing page shows per-route latency and token cost breakdown. top left is the embeddings route, you can see a heat map of payload sizes and a suggestions tab from Optimize. apologies if the model name shows slightly different - some auto transcript label might call it 'Redwood model rf-embed-1' or similar.
02:38 Ethan Park: (typing) sample curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rf-embed-1","inputs":["document text...","user query..."]}' response returns embedding vectors, id, meta. For rerank: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"rf-rerank-1","query":"user query","candidates":[{"id":1,"text":"doc A"},...] }' returns a score list kept small to keep latency low.
03:15 Priya Singh: that matches what we want. how many candidates do you recommend sending to rerank? we currently send top 100 from opensearch which is slow.
03:24 Ethan Park: top 100 is heavy - we typically recommend sending 10-30 candidates for rerank to keep latency low; then use hybrid heuristics: vector similarity threshold + bm25 to prefilter. that reduces rerank compute and still covers recall. also suggest caching the top-K embeddings for frequent queries.
03:45 Liam O'Connor: ok. for our regulatory team, we need SOC2 + audit logs, encryption at rest with KMS, and EMEA data residency - are those covered by hosted?
03:58 Maya Chen: yes - hosted API is SOC2-compliant (we maintain SOC2 reports), we support customer-specific KMS integrations for private and dedicated deployments; hosted can use region-based controls to keep data in eu-west regions, but for strict residency or on-prem you could go Private. i'll attach our security packet after the call.
04:17 Noah Patel: any caveats about PII redaction or retention windows? our security team wants 30 day retention only.
04:25 Maya Chen: you can configure retention windows and opt out of data logging for enterprise tiers; default hosted may keep short logs for debugging but enterprise contracts support shorter windows and no retention with a PR. we'll include the options in the packet.
04:38 Priya Singh: can you run a quick demo with a small sample corpus so we can see rerank scores change?
04:45 Ethan Park: sure - i'm going to pull a 10 doc sample. apologies for background noise, there's a small echo - transcript may pick it up.
05:00 [demo run - embedding + similarity queries] 05:04 Ethan Park: okay first call, embedding the corpus - you can see vectors return inline, embedding dims 1536 for rf-embed-1 in this example. then a search query does nearest neighbors, we pass top 20 candidates to rerank.
05:25 Ethan Park: rerank returns ranked list with scores, see how doc that was earlier low in bm25 jumps up because the rerank model picks up context. latency 94ms for rerank here, embedding call 48ms, total ~142ms.
05:47 Priya Singh: nice, that's within our bar. question: how do you handle model updates/versioning? we need stable outputs for A/B testing.
05:57 Maya Chen: we have model pinning and versioned routes, you can pin model versions per route or rollout canaries via the console. console also stores per-prompt evals and you can tie regression alerts to test sets in Optimize.
06:13 Liam O'Connor: curious about scaling - if we run a pilot with 50 qps, any recommendations on concurrency and batching?
06:20 Ethan Park: For 50 qps, we recommend batching embeddings into 16-32 item batches where possible - if queries are low-latency sensitive we prefer small batches but continuous batching helps cost. for rerank, because candidate set is small, concurrency matters more; dedicated pools help if you need consistent 95p latency under load.
06:44 Noah Patel: do you support SSO / SAML for console access? we prefer enterprise SSO + RBAC.
06:50 Maya Chen: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC for fine-grained roles. audit logs shipped to your SIEM if you want. we'll list the integrations in the security packet.
07:02 Priya Singh: any limitations on document size for embeddings? our docs can be long (~8k chars).
07:10 Ethan Park: we recommend chunking larger docs (2k-4k char chunks) and storing chunk metadata; Optimize will suggest chunk sizes that balance recall vs cost. we can show recommended chunking heuristics in the benchmark plan.
07:25 [brief pause, minor crosstalk] 07:33 Liam O'Connor: what about offline/air-gapped requirements? some of our legal folks ask about on-prem options.
07:39 Maya Chen: for strict air-gapped or on-prem, Redwood Private is the option - it's a customer-managed control plane and can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem (with our on-prem package). that comes with a different licensing model; i'll include the enterprise pricing sheet.
07:55 Priya Singh: re: cost - can you show an example cost breakdown for a 100k monthly queries scenario?
08:02 Maya Chen: i don't have the live calculator up here but i'll send a sample TCO spreadsheet - it will show per-embedding unit cost, rerank per-call, plus estimated savings from caching/batching as suggested by Optimize.
08:18 Ethan Park: also note model choice affects unit cost - smaller embed models are cheaper but may reduce quality; Optimize can run small evals on your test set and recommend the best tradeoff.
08:31 Priya Singh: are there pre-built connectors for our vector DB? we're currently using OpenSearch's vector plugin.
08:36 Ethan Park: we have SDKs and examples for OpenSearch, Pinecone, Milvus and plain Postgres/FAISS flows. for OpenSearch we have recommended hybrid queries and prefilter hooks you can drop into your pipeline.
08:50 Noah Patel: on the rerank model side, do you provide explainability scores or tokens that influenced rank?
08:58 Ethan Park: rerank returns scores and optional explain metadata (highlight spans) in enterprise tiers; there's also a reason-code feature in debug mode but not always turned on in low-latency paths. will note that in the security/ops doc.
09:12 [demo: console - Optimize recommendations tab] 09:20 Ethan Park: Optimize here highlights batching suggestions - shows estimated cost reduction 28% if you batch X per minute and cache top-K. it also recommends a quantized rerank model variant for cheaper ops if quality drop is acceptable.
09:42 Priya Singh: good. our latency requirement is 95p <200ms for search. you said hosted may hit that; can you guarantee SLA?
09:50 Maya Chen: hosted has standard SLAs for availability; latency SLOs we provide guidance on and can meet enterprise goals with dedicated or reserved capacity and region pinning. SLA for latency can be part of a dedicated contract.
10:06 Liam O'Connor: anything else about logging and data deletion workflows - we want to be able to prove deletion requests are honored for GDPR.
10:13 Maya Chen: yes, deletion APIs exist, we keep audit logs and can provide attestation for deletion as part of the enterprise agreement.
10:20 [15 minute mark - mid-call recap] 10:22 Maya Chen: quick recap - demo showed embed + rerank flow, Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, security coverage SOC2/KMS/SSO, Private option for on-prem. Next steps: i'll send pricing/security packet, ethan will prep benchmark plan, you (BrightFind) will upload sample data.
10:38 Priya Singh: sounds good. two extra technical questions: (1) can you do rerank with additional context like user history, and (2) how do you deal with cold-start caching?
10:48 Ethan Park: (1) yes you can pass auxiliary context fields - we allow up to N kb in the rerank payload, and you can attach structured context; (2) cold-start we use prefix/KV caching and warm-up heuristics; Optimize can detect frequent queries and recommend pre-caching or scheduled warm-up.
11:05 Noah Patel: for the pilot, can we do a weekly sync and a mid-pilot check-in with your se?
11:10 Maya Chen: absolutely - we'll propose a cadence in the follow-up.
11:15 Liam O'Connor: any known gotchas migrating from OpenSearch + self-embeds to hosted?
11:20 Ethan Park: biggest is chunking strategy and prefilter thresholds - you may need to tune recall vs precision. also watch costs for naive per-request embeddings - caching and batch pre-computes usually fix that. we'll help with migration playbook.
11:35 Priya Singh: do you have a public SDK for python and node? our team uses python.
11:40 Maya Chen: yes python and node SDKs with examples for embedding ingestion, rerank flow and console integration. we'll point to github repos in the follow-up.
11:50 [closing minutes - commercial questions] 11:55 Noah Patel: ok commercially we prefer a 3-month pilot with committed throughput and an option to convert to dedicated if results look good.
12:03 Maya Chen: that's a common flow - pilot to validate recall/latency and then move to dedicated reserved capacity or Private if you need residency. i'll outline pilot terms in the pricing doc.
12:12 Liam O'Connor: fine. anything else from your side?
12:16 Maya Chen: no, thanks for the time. again i'll send: pricing + enterprise security packet (SOC2/ISO reports, KMS details), ethan will share the benchmark plan and sample payload guidelines, and we'll schedule kickoff week of 7/29.
12:28 Priya Singh: thanks everyone.
12:30 [call end - 48 mins total per recording]
